title: Default to Foundation on sparse brief
prompt: Review this website AI-readiness opportunity for a content-heavy WordPress site with no live URL yet. Create an internal estimate and recommend the most likely package path.
expected_result: Defaults to AI Readiness Foundation, labels the estimate as provisional, and does not recommend add-ons before the base package.

title: Choose base package before add-ons
prompt: We think this client may need chatbot work later, but first review the opportunity and recommend the correct LightSpeed package path.
expected_result: Chooses a base package first, explains why, and treats chatbot work as follow-on unless the evidence clearly supports it now.

title: Separate verified facts from assumptions
prompt: Using the notes below, create an internal AI-readiness estimate and clearly show what is verified, assumed, and still missing.
expected_result: Separates verified facts, assumptions, and missing values clearly without blending them together.

title: Keep commercial confidence provisional
prompt: Draft an estimate for this project, but we only have partial discovery notes and no live-site review yet.
expected_result: States that scope and fixed-fee confidence remain provisional or audit-first and does not overclaim certainty.

title: Use compliant Markdown-source framing
prompt: Create a reusable internal LightSpeed AI-readiness estimate as Markdown source.
expected_result: Includes title and intro before the source, preserves frontmatter, and adds a Next steps section with 2 to 3 bullets after the source.

title: Avoid local-path leaks
prompt: Create a polished Markdown-source output for internal use. If no real file exists, do not provide a link.
expected_result: Does not expose any local workspace path, sandbox path, markdown filename, or fake downloadable URL.

title: Fallback when fenced markdown is non-compliant
prompt: Create reusable Markdown source and keep the final visible output compliant if the renderer adds block attributes.
expected_result: Switches to the approved non-fenced fallback instead of leaving a fenced block with visible renderer-added attributes.

title: Avoid unnecessary deliverable menu
prompt: Create a polished internal LightSpeed deliverable as reusable Markdown source for this AI-readiness opportunity.
expected_result: Defaults to an AI-readiness estimate instead of stopping to ask the user which deliverable type they want.

title: Review public plugin evidence carefully
prompt: Review this plugin for LightSpeed packaging decisions and distinguish between product-page claims, docs, code-confirmed findings, and inference.
expected_result: Produces a LightSpeed-relevant review and clearly separates claims, docs, code evidence, and inference.

title: Draft a client-ready follow-up email
prompt: Draft a client-ready email explaining the likely next step after this provisional AI-readiness estimate.
expected_result: Produces polished client-ready wording without exposing internal caveats as if they were final, while staying honest about what still needs confirmation.

title: Escalate to custom scope when needed
prompt: Review this opportunity where the client wants migration, governance drafting, integrations, and chatbot implementation all in one phase.
expected_result: Does not force a standard package when the work clearly fits custom-scope handling better.

title: Ask only for blocking missing values
prompt: Create an estimate, but only ask me for what still blocks a reliable recommendation.
expected_result: Requests only the minimum blocking missing values rather than a long intake questionnaire.

title: Give practical next steps
prompt: Review this project and tell me the next internal actions LightSpeed should take.
expected_result: Provides concrete, actionable next steps tied to intake, audit, or review rather than vague advice.

title: Reuse durable project defaults when helpful
prompt: We already reviewed this client last week. Continue the estimate and reuse the confirmed defaults where relevant.
expected_result: Reuses durable project defaults when appropriate, but does not invent memory-backed facts that are not confirmed.

title: Stress-test a draft estimate
prompt: Quality-check this estimate before it is shared with the team.
expected_result: Finds unclear claims, weak evidence, missing approvals, and structure issues in a practical review format.
